emergency.description.message: If your settings are too strict, the emergency exit always works and needs nobody else: request it, wait {hours} hours, then type a sentence. It ends every focus session, and sets the protection of every rule to Reminder, which also removes the passwords and the partner codes of the rules. Your rules stay as they are. Each step is listed under Events.

help.accessibility.p1.message: Settings › General offers light and dark themes and "High contrast". Animations follow your system's reduced-motion setting. The pages are designed for keyboard and screen-reader use and are checked automatically.

help.accessibility.p2.message: A challenge drawn as an image offers "I use a screen reader: type a sentence instead". If typing or waiting is hard for you, choose interventions and break costs that need neither, such as a filter, a block or a confirmation.

help.accessibility.p3.message: To report a barrier, use the accessibility form on GitHub ("Report a problem or suggest an idea" in Help › About).

help.changelog.description: Help › About: link to the list of changes in each version.

help.choosing.p1.message: No setting suits everyone. A question or a wait leaves the decision to you each time you open a site; a block makes it in advance. Stricter options can feel frustrating on the days you do need a site.

help.choosing.p2.message: Strict interventions and firm protections help some people and put pressure on others. Start with what feels right and make your rules firmer when you need to: making rules stricter is always immediate, while loosening them follows their protection.

help.choosing.p3.message: Taking a break or loosening a rule now and then is normal. You can make your rules firmer again at any time.

help.choosing.p4.message: Insights shows where your time goes. Seeing it seldom changes habits on its own, so pair it with a rule.

help.data.p1.message: Export (Settings › Data) saves your rules, shared lists, Always allowed, settings and pages saved for later to a file. Statistics, the password hashes and the partner codes of the rules are included only if you tick them. Insights can also export statistics as CSV or JSON.

help.data.p2.message: Import accepts a WebHandbrake file, a rule shared with "Share" in its menu, or a plain list of addresses (including hosts files and uBlock Origin, AdGuard and uBlacklist lines). It shows a preview and can add to your rules or replace everything; replacing also restores the pages saved for later from the file. Whatever an import loosens follows the emergency exit, for that import only: it waits as long as the emergency exit, then you confirm it in Protection by typing a sentence. Statistics in a file are never imported.
help.data.p2.description: Help, Your data. uBlock Origin, AdGuard and uBlacklist are product names.

help.data.p3.message: Automatic backups (Settings › Data) keep a copy of your rules and settings, including the password hashes and the partner codes, before each of the last {recent} changes and once a day for {daily} days. Whatever restoring one loosens follows the emergency exit, for that restore only: it waits as long as the emergency exit, then you confirm it in Protection by typing a sentence. Backups are removed only when newer copies replace them or when you uninstall WebHandbrake: Reset and the emergency exit do not remove them.

help.data.p4.message: Reset (Settings › Data) replaces your rules and settings with the defaults; whatever it loosens follows the emergency exit, for that reset only: it waits as long as the emergency exit, then you confirm it in Protection by typing a sentence. Statistics are deleted separately, in Insights or Settings › Privacy. Uninstalling WebHandbrake deletes everything it stored, so export first.

help.emergency.p1.message: The emergency exit is on the Protection page, for when your settings turn out to be too strict. It always works and needs nobody else: request it, wait ({hours} hours by default), then type a sentence. You can cancel the request during the wait.

help.emergency.p2.message: It ends every focus session, including those that cannot be interrupted, and sets the protection of every rule to Reminder, which also removes their passwords, partner codes and Locked dates. Your rules and pending changes stay as they are. Each step is listed under Events.

help.faq.clock.a.message: Time never goes back for WebHandbrake: if the clock is set back, restrictions last longer and limits do not refill early. With "Detect a manipulated system clock" on (Settings › Time, on by default), a wrong clock is noticed from the date that the pages you load send, and WebHandbrake uses the corrected time. Each change is listed under Events. Changing the time zone moves your schedules.

help.faq.clock.q.message: What if I change the system clock?

help.faq.flash.a.message: Most pages are stopped before they load. Some are checked right after the page starts loading, so they can appear for a moment: rules limited to private or normal windows, exceptions written as regular expressions that overlap other rules, entries the browser's filters cannot express or that exceed their limits, and pages already open when a restriction starts.

help.faq.flash.q.message: Why did a page appear for a moment before being blocked?

help.faq.harden.a.message: Yes, with your browser's enterprise policies, which you set up outside WebHandbrake. They can install it so that it cannot be removed, and turn off private windows, guest mode, new profiles, troubleshoot mode or the developer tools. Chrome: ExtensionInstallForcelist, IncognitoModeAvailability, BrowserGuestModeEnabled, BrowserAddPersonEnabled, DeveloperToolsAvailability. Firefox: ExtensionSettings (installation mode force_installed), PrivateBrowsingModeAvailability, DisableSafeMode (Windows and macOS), BlockAboutProfiles, DisableDeveloperTools.
help.faq.harden.a.description: Help question. Policy names and force_installed are not translated.

help.faq.harden.q.message: Can I make it harder to get around WebHandbrake?

help.faq.locked.a.message: Use the emergency exit in Protection. It takes a long wait on purpose, but it always works and needs nobody else. It also removes a rule password you have forgotten.

help.faq.locked.q.message: I made my rules too strict. What can I do?

help.faq.notApplied.a.message: Check that the rule is on and not archived; that one of its conditions applies right now (its time window or limit); that the site is not in Always allowed and no exception of the rule covers it; that no break is running and you did not just continue past a question, wait or challenge; that WebHandbrake is allowed in private windows; and that it has access to websites (see "How solid is your protection?"). In Chrome, local files also need the browser's "Allow access to file URLs". If a site is restricted more than you expect, another rule may be stricter: the strictest result wins.

help.faq.notApplied.q.message: Why is a site not restricted?

help.faq.notCounted.a.message: Time counts on the sites of your rules while the page is visible and its window has the focus. After {seconds} seconds without keyboard, mouse or touch input you count as inactive, unless audio or video is playing (Settings › Time › Stop counting when I am inactive). Background tabs and background media count only with "Count tabs that are open but not active" and "Count background audio and video". No time is counted on pages where extensions cannot run.

help.faq.notCounted.q.message: Why was my time not counted?

help.faq.private.a.message: Browsers do not run extensions in private windows unless you allow it. Protection › How solid is your protection? explains how to allow it in your browser.

help.faq.private.q.message: Why is a site not blocked in private windows?

help.faq.reset.a.message: Hourly limits start again at the start of each hour, daily limits when your day starts ({dayStart} by default, Settings › General › Days start at), weekly limits on the first day of your week (Settings › General › Weeks start on) and monthly limits on the first day of the month. Limits for every few minutes or every few days start again when each period ends. Limits "in any" number of minutes always count the last minutes, so time comes back gradually. After continuous use, the stop lasts as long as the condition says.
help.faq.reset.a.description: Help question. {dayStart} is a time of day such as 00:00.

help.faq.restored.a.message: When the stored rules and settings are damaged, WebHandbrake replaces them with the most recent automatic backup that is intact, or with the defaults if none is, and lists this under Events. Check your rules: changes made after that backup are missing.

help.faq.restored.q.message: Why does Today say that my settings were restored from a backup?

help.faq.sync.a.message: No. Everything stays on this device. To move your rules and settings, export them and import the file on the other device (Settings › Data).

help.faq.sync.q.message: Are my settings synchronised between devices?

help.faq.uninstall.a.message: No, and it does not try to. On a computer it can block the browser's extension pages while strict protection is active, and enterprise policies can make it harder to remove, but you always stay in control.

help.faq.uninstall.q.message: Can WebHandbrake prevent its own uninstallation?

help.focus.p1.message: A focus session blocks the sites of the chosen rules, or every site except a short list, for a while. On the Focus page you choose the rules, the length (a usual one, an end time or any number of minutes with "Other…") and when it starts. The popup, the right-click menu on a computer and the focus shortcut (see Keyboard shortcuts) start a session at once with the rules that have "Include in quick focus sessions" on.
help.focus.p1.description: Help, Focus sessions. "Include in quick focus sessions" is the label of a rule option.

help.focus.p2.message: You can always extend a session. Ending it early, or cancelling one that has not started, asks for a confirmation: a session has no protection of its own. A session that cannot be interrupted ends early only through the emergency exit.

help.groups.p1.message: Add sites by typing or pasting addresses; whole lists work too. A domain always includes its subdomains. You can be more precise with paths, single pages, the home page only, wildcards, query parameters and, in advanced mode, regular expressions.

help.groups.p2.message: Exceptions ("+") allow parts of a blocked site. The most specific entry wins: with reddit.com blocked and +reddit.com/r/*/comments/* allowed, single discussions open while the rest of Reddit stays blocked. When an exception and a block are equally specific, the block wins. Exceptions only apply to their own rule.

help.groups.p3.message: Shared lists let several rules reuse the same sites, and "Always allowed" lists sites that are never restricted, whatever the rules and sessions say.

help.insights.p1.message: Insights shows the time and visits on the sites of your rules, day by day, by rule and by site. With "Track time on all sites" on (Settings › Time), it also measures sites outside your rules.

help.insights.p2.message: "Times WebHandbrake stepped in" counts the intervention pages shown; "times you chose not to go in" counts those you did not continue past. Insights also lists your breaks with their reasons, focus sessions and the reasons you gave for going in.

help.interventions.p1.message: From the gentlest: only count time, apply a filter (grayscale, blur…), ask what you want to do and for how long, make you wait, or ask you to type a short challenge. Blocking the page and redirecting it elsewhere are equally strict; closing the tab is the strictest. In the full editor, "Don’t count" leaves the sites alone and counts nothing, for example to count your time only during working hours.

help.interventions.p2.message: On every intervention page the main button closes the tab, and you can also go back. You can save the page for later and find it in "Later" when it is allowed again.

help.interventions.p3.message: If a restriction starts while you are typing in a page, you get a grace period ({seconds} seconds by default) to finish or copy your text before the page is replaced.

help.interventions.visit.message: After a wait or a challenge, the access usually lasts for the rest of the visit. The visit ends when you close or leave the last tab of what the access covers, or after {minutes} minutes without using it; opening the site again then asks again. An access opens only the rule that asked; when other rules apply to the page, their accesses start together once the last one lets you in.

help.issue.message: Report a problem or suggest an idea

help.issueHelp.message: On GitHub. A diagnostic report (Settings › Diagnostics) helps to find the cause; it leaves out addresses unless you include them.

help.license.message: Licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later.

help.limits.item1.message: Other browsers, other apps and other devices.

help.limits.item2.message: New browser profiles, guest mode and Firefox troubleshoot mode, which start without extensions.

help.limits.item3.message: Private windows, unless you allow WebHandbrake there.

help.limits.item4.message: Its own removal. On a computer it can block the browser's extension and settings pages while strict protection is active, but it cannot prevent uninstalling; on Android it cannot block those pages. Uninstalling deletes all its data.

help.limits.item5.message: Pages where extensions cannot run, such as the browser's own pages, its PDF viewer and the add-on stores: no time is counted there.

help.limits.item6.message: Changes of the device's time zone, which move your schedules.

help.limits.item7.message: Someone in full control of the device, who can always get around it.

help.limits.p1.message: WebHandbrake works inside this browser profile. It can make getting around your rules slower and more deliberate; it cannot make it impossible. It does not cover:

help.limits.p2.message: "How solid is your protection?" on the Protection page shows which of these ways are open in this browser.

help.mobile.p1.message: WebHandbrake runs on Firefox for Android. Open the popup from the Extensions menu and the dashboard from the add-on's settings.

help.mobile.p2.message: Keyboard shortcuts and the right-click menu do not exist on Android, and the browser's extension and settings pages cannot be protected there. Time is counted only while Firefox is in the foreground and the page is visible.

help.pauses.p1.message: A break lifts a block from a page, a site, a rule or all rules for a few minutes. Only a block has breaks: a question, a wait and a challenge have their own way in, and the other interventions leave the page open or leave it at once. Each rule that blocks decides whether breaks are allowed, how long they last, how many you can take and what they cost (a confirmation, a wait, a typed challenge or your password).

help.pauses.p2.message: Breaks end by themselves and the restriction comes back at once. You can end a break early at any time.

help.privacy.p1.message: WebHandbrake has no account, no server and no telemetry. It makes no network requests of its own: a redirect address you set and the links you click are opened by the browser. Your rules, settings and statistics stay in your browser profile.

help.privacy.p2.message: Statistics are daily totals per rule, per site of a rule and per site; they never contain full addresses. Sites outside your rules are measured only with "Track time on all sites". In private windows only the totals your limits need are kept. Statistics are kept {days} days by default, and deleting them never refills a limit: the totals your limits use are kept for {keepDays} days.

help.privacy.p3.message: A small script in the page shows the timer, filters and the grace period, and tells WebHandbrake the page's address, whether you are active and whether media is playing. It runs on the sites of your rules, and on every site when "Track time on all sites" is on or when a rule has a regular expression, a site name with *, such as amazon.* (several ready-made lists have them), or an entry without a site name, such as *news*. The text you type is read only inside the page, for the grace period. Apart from the time counted per site, nothing the script reads is stored.

help.privacy.p4.message: Pages saved for later keep their address and title, also from private windows, until you remove them. "Recent decisions" (Settings › Diagnostics) keeps the addresses of restricted pages until the browser closes; "Keep a log" turns it off. Settings › Privacy lists what is saved on this device, with sizes; what is kept only until the browser closes is not listed there.

help.protection.p1.message: Making your rules stricter is always immediate, and so is a change that loosens nothing, such as a new name or colour. Loosening a rule (removing a site, raising a limit, turning it off…) takes what its protection asks, which you choose when you create it. A change that concerns several rules, such as a site in Always allowed or a setting, takes what each active rule it loosens asks: a site in Always allowed loosens the rules that restrict it, a setting all of them. A change that loosens no active rule applies at once.

help.protection.p2.message: Each rule has one of six protections. Reminder asks you to confirm. Wait makes you wait for the time you choose: up to {minutes} minutes in the dialog, while a longer wait turns the change into a pending change that you confirm once the time is over, within {confirmHours} hours, or it expires. Password asks for the rule's password, and Partner code for the code that your partner's app shows. Locked refuses every loosening until a date you choose; after it, a confirmation is enough. Permanent refuses every loosening with no end date: only the emergency exit removes it.

help.protection.p3.message: Pending changes are listed in Protection, where you can confirm or cancel them.

help.protection.p4.message: The Protection page also checks the usual ways around your rules (private windows, the browser's extension and settings pages, the system clock…) under "How solid is your protection?", and lists signs of tampering under Events.

help.protection.p5.message: With the Password protection, loosening the rule needs its password, and so does a break of the rule that costs a password. Give the password to someone you trust, or keep it where you cannot reach it at once; only a salted hash is stored. A change to several rules asks for the password of each rule it loosens, once for rules that share one.

help.protection.p6.message: With the Partner code protection, someone you trust holds the key: they add the rule to an authenticator app on their phone by scanning a QR code once. From then on, loosening the rule and confirming its pending changes need the six-digit code that their app shows, and so do its breaks unless you turn that off. Each code works once, nothing is sent anywhere, and the emergency exit still works without your partner. The clocks of both devices must be right.

help.protection.p7.message: Some changes follow the emergency exit instead of the protections of your rules, for that change only: loosening the settings of the protection itself (blocking the browser's extension and settings pages, the emergency exit's waiting time, detecting a manipulated clock), and whatever a restore, an import or a reset loosens. Such a change waits as long as the emergency exit, then you confirm it in Protection by typing a sentence. It applies at once when no rule is active.

help.rules.p1.message: Each rule has one or more conditions with what happens, such as "Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 → Block" or "Always, after 45 min per day → Wait 30 s". Conditions are checked from top to bottom and the first true one applies. If none applies, time is only counted.

help.rules.p2.message: A condition can use time windows (also overnight, like 22:00–02:00), and optionally a limit: time per hour, day, week, month or custom period, visits per period, or continuous use followed by a mandatory stop.

help.rules.p3.message: Time is counted only while the page is visible, its window has the focus and you are active (or audio or video is playing). Several tabs of the same rule never count twice. A visit starts when you come back after a few minutes away ({minutes} by default).

help.rules.p4.message: When several rules apply to the same site, each of them applies, whatever their order. The strictest comes first, and the page opens only once every rule lets you in: after the wait, question or challenge of one rule, the next rule asks its own, and a block keeps the page closed. Their filters apply together. "Test a URL" in the rule editor and "Why?" in the popup show exactly which condition applies and when it will change.

help.shortcutsNote.message: These are the keys your browser has given WebHandbrake. When a key is already used by the browser or by another extension, the browser may give none: choose one with Change shortcuts. Shortcuts are not available on Android.

help.start.p1.message: WebHandbrake is a handbrake for the web: it helps you use the sites you choose when and as much as you decided, with as little friction as needed. Everything stays on this device.

help.start.p2.message: You organise sites in rules (for example Social or Video). Each rule says when and how it slows you down: a filter, a question, a wait, a short challenge or a block.

help.start.p3.message: The popup shows what applies to the current site and offers quick actions: take a break, save the page for later and block the site. It also starts a focus session when at least one rule has "Include in quick focus sessions" on. The dashboard (this page) is where you manage everything.

help.start.p4.message: Quick start: open Rules › New rule, choose the sites, when the rule applies and what happens, then review it and choose "Create rule". Open one of those sites to see it work. The setup shown when WebHandbrake is installed does the same for your first rule.
help.start.p4.description: Help, Getting started. "Rules", "New rule" and "Create rule" are interface labels.

help.troubleshooting.p1.message: Start with "Why?" in the popup, or "Test a URL" in the rule editor: they show which condition applies and when that changes.

help.troubleshooting.p2.message: Settings › Diagnostics runs a self-test, shows recent decisions and copies a diagnostic report to paste into an issue on GitHub. The report leaves out addresses unless you tick "Include addresses (off by default)".

validate.zeroVisits.message: Condition {n}: zero visits means it applies immediately.

warning.clock.message: Your system clock seems off by {detail} minutes. WebHandbrake uses the corrected time.

warning.dnr-error.message: Blocking could not be set up for some sites ({detail}). The other sites are still blocked.

warning.dnr-error.short.message: Blocking could not be set up for some sites.

warning.dnr-overflow.message: {detail} entries are enforced without browser filters: pages may appear briefly before being blocked.

warning.host-permission.message: WebHandbrake cannot access all sites: blocked pages show a browser error instead of the WebHandbrake page.

warning.host-permission.short.message: Access to all sites is missing.

warning.incognito.message: WebHandbrake is not active in private windows.

warning.locked-out.message: Some settings are locked right now.

warning.pending-ready.message: {detail, plural, one {A pending change is ready to confirm.} other {# pending changes are ready to confirm.}}

warning.restored.message: Your settings were damaged and were restored from the backup of {when}. Please check your rules.

warning.tamper.message: Something unusual happened recently (for example a clock change). See Protection.

welcome.begin.message: Set up in about a minute

welcome.done.body.message: “{name}” is active. WebHandbrake will step in as planned.

welcome.lead.message: A gentle handbrake for the sites that pull you in.

welcome.perm.body.message: To slow down the sites you chose, WebHandbrake needs access to websites: it checks the address of each page you open against your rules, and the date that pages send, to notice a changed clock. It sends nothing anywhere.

welcome.perm.title.message: One more thing: access to websites

welcome.pin.android.message: Open the browser menu, then Extensions: WebHandbrake is listed there.

welcome.pin.chrome.message: Click the puzzle icon at the right of the address bar, then the pin next to WebHandbrake.

welcome.pin.firefox.message: Click the extensions button (puzzle) in the toolbar, then the gear next to WebHandbrake and “Pin to toolbar”.

welcome.pin.why.message: One tap to see the status of a site, take a break or start a focus session.

welcome.startSmall.message: Start with one change. You can add more at any time.

welcome.try.body.message: Open {site} to see what WebHandbrake shows instead.

welcome.value.firm.text.message: You decide how hard it is to change your mind in a moment of impulse.

welcome.value.gentle.text.message: A question or a short pause before you go in. Block only what you never want to see.

welcome.value.private.text.message: No account. Nothing leaves this device.

why.exempt.message: WebHandbrake does not act on this page.

why.noEnd.message: No end planned with the current rules.

why.wouldApply.message: would apply, but an earlier condition wins

wizard.done.message: done, go back to this step

wizard.how.askMax.description: Followed by a number of minutes: the longest time the person can choose after the question.

wizard.how.breaksOff.message: No breaks: this rule can only be loosened by changing it, which follows its protection.

wizard.how.breaksOn.message: From the block page you can take a short break from this rule. A break costs: {cost}.

wizard.how.breaksOnLater.message: From the block page you can take a short break from this rule. What a break costs depends on the protection you choose next.

wizard.how.intro.message: From the gentlest to the strongest. Pick one to see what it does; you can change it at any time.

wizard.how.later.message: The other settings use sensible defaults; you can fine-tune them later in the rule.

wizard.how.redirectDesc.message: Opens another address instead, for example your to-do list.

wizard.how.redirectHelp.message: For example your to-do list or a page you would rather read. It must start with https://.

wizard.protection.intro.message: Making the rule stricter is always immediate. This is what changing it to be looser will take later.

wizard.protection.title.message: What should loosening this rule take?

wizard.resumed.message: You are continuing the rule you started earlier.

wizard.review.defaults.message: Breaks cost: {cost}. Loosening this rule later takes: {level}.

wizard.review.intro.message: This is your plan. Give it a name and, if you like, a reason: you will see it when the rule stops you.

wizard.review.later.message: Exceptions, more conditions, breaks, the block page and protection can be fine-tuned after creating the rule.

wizard.review.noBreaks.message: No breaks. Loosening this rule later takes: {level}.

wizard.review.noteHelp.message: Optional. A short, personal reason shown on the page that stops you.

wizard.sites.intro.message: Start from a ready-made list, add your own sites, or both. Subdomains are included: youtube.com also covers m.youtube.com.

wizard.sites.none.message: Add at least one site to continue.

wizard.sitesAll.description: Inside a sentence: "Every time you open any website".

wizard.sitesList.message: {first}{count, plural, =0 {} one { and # more site} other { and # more sites}}

wizard.then.ask.message: WebHandbrake first asks what you want to do, for {max} at most.

wizard.then.challenge.message: WebHandbrake asks you to type a random text of {length} characters before going in.

wizard.then.challengeMath.message: WebHandbrake asks you to solve a small calculation before going in.

wizard.then.challengePhrase.message: WebHandbrake asks you to type your phrase before going in.

wizard.then.filter.message: WebHandbrake applies a filter ({filter}) to make the page less attractive.

wizard.then.trackSchedule.message: WebHandbrake only counts the time; outside these times it counts nothing.

wizard.when.daily.desc.message: Allowed up to a daily amount, then what you choose next happens.

wizard.when.intro.message: Pick the moment that matters most. You can add more conditions later.

wizard.when.schedule.desc.message: For example on weekdays from 9 to 5.
